summary: Goat Peak's later lookout cab was sold in 1969 and moved to the Teanaway Valley, Kittitas County, where it sits on a hill visible from Teanaway Road.

facts.design: 10-ft treated timber R-6 flat-roof lookout, which replaced the 1928 D-6 cupola cabin on Goat Peak (replacement date disputed)

access.note: Sold in 1969 to a local family (WTA). WTA says it can be seen from Teanaway Road, on a hill behind the Teanaway general store. No source found describes public access.

visit.trail_note: View from Teanaway Road only (WTA). The cab went to a local family, so do not go onto the property.

events.note: 1927 allotments included $800 for a lookout house on Goat Peak (The Leavenworth Echo, as quoted by Forest Lookouts).
First lookout on Goat Peak, a D-6 cupola cabin (original site).
WTA: a new R-6 flat cabin on a treated 10-ft tower was built in 1956, after an L-4 cabin in the late 1930s.
Register and firelookout.com: the 10-ft treated timber R-6 flat tower replaced the cupola cabin about 1960. Conflicts with WTA's 1956.
Sold and moved to the Teanaway Valley. WTA says a local family took it apart to move it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com put the 10-ft R-6 tower at about 1960; WTA says 1956 and adds an L-4 cabin in the late 1930s. Not resolved; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 'relocated' event has no year; 1969 is from four sources. The story is about the moved cab; the original site is us-wa-goat-peak-2. The replacement-date conflict (1956 WTA vs about 1960 register and firelookout.com) and the WTA-only L-4 interim cab are unresolved. A different Goat Peak lookout, an NHLR entry in the Methow River valley dated 1923 that appeared in search results, was not used and should not be merged with this one. The geocaching page for this lookout returned only its title, so it was not used. No public access was found.
